description: Invented teaching dates, premiums and fees. These are not actual FOMC meetings, market quotes or investment recommendations. All changes are basis points; every digital pays $0 or $1.

examples.name: matched_two_state
examples.description: A full calendar loading of 1 and four short spread lots require exactly 4,167 long upper-state digital contracts. The two specified states produce the same net payoff after the same explicit costs.

examples.name: integer_rounding
examples.description: One short spread lot requires 1,041.75 long digitals. Rounding to 1,042 leaves a $0.25 upper-minus-lower endpoint residual. The fee example explicitly applies a quadratic coefficient and rounds its total upward to cents.

examples.name: unhedged_tail
examples.description: The same exact two-state hedge is exposed to an increase of 50 bp. This synthetic upper-bucket digital still pays only $1 at 50 bp; it cannot offset the extra linear futures loss. The tail payout is an explicit input, not an assumption about a real contract.

examples.name: other_decisions_cancelled
examples.description: The target effective on April 16 has loading 1/2 in April-minus-May. A prior March decision affects both delivery months equally; a June decision affects neither. Eight short spread lots therefore require exactly 4,167 long digitals, and changing the other decisions does not change the package payoff.

scenarios.name: Target lower state; other changes zero
Target upper state; other changes zero

examples.name: other_decision_uncancelled
examples.description: An additional decision effective May 16 affects the far month but not the near month, leaving loading 16/31. The target two-state endpoints still match while the other decision is fixed, but this digital alone cannot hedge the independently varying other decision.

scenarios.name: Target lower; other fixed at zero
Target upper; other fixed at zero
